blurb: Tiny toy dog with a long, silky pure-white coat that falls straight to the ground
description: The Maltese is a toy companion breed linked to Italy and Malta, weighing 3–4 kg, with a silky pure-white coat and a lively, affectionate nature.
answer: The Maltese is a toy companion breed with a long, silky, pure-white coat, hanging ears and a tail curved over its back, recognized by the FCI under the patronage of Italy. Its name recalls an ancient small white dog associated with the island of Malta, though the modern breed was shaped in the Victorian era. It weighs about 3–4 kg and is described as lively, calm and affectionate.

body: Small dogs called Melitaean were among the favorite pets of ancient Greece and Rome, with writers linking them to Malta or the Adriatic island of Mljet. Genomic experts say the modern Maltese cannot be traced by pedigree to these dogs and instead emerged in the Victorian era, related to the Bichon, Bolognese and Havanese. A Maltese class appeared at a London show in 1862, the American Kennel Club recognized the breed in 1888, and the FCI accepted it in 1955.

The coat is dense, glossy and silky, falling heavily along the body without curls or an undercoat. The color is pure white, though a pale ivory tinge or light brown spotting is permitted. Adults usually weigh 3–4 kg, with females about 20–23 cm tall and males slightly taller.
The Maltese is described as lively, calm and affectionate. It is kept for companionship, ornament or competitive exhibition.

The Maltese is described as not shedding, and like other white dogs it may show tear stains. Sources give little detail on grooming routines or exercise, though the long coat is generally expected to need regular attention.

Conditions reported in the breed include liver and heart problems, luxating patella and patent ductus arteriosus. A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.1 years, and a 2024 Italian study found 11 years.

faq.q: How big does a Maltese get?
faq.a: Maltese are very small, typically about 20–25 cm tall and 3–4 kg in weight.
The Maltese is described as not shedding; its coat has no undercoat.

faq.q: How long do Maltese dogs live?
faq.a: A commonly cited figure is about 15 years; a 2024 UK study found 13.1 years and an Italian study 11 years.

faq.q: Is the Maltese recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists the Maltese as breed number 65 in Group 9, companion and toy dogs.
